title: Saturday-night fish fries with guitar music
summary: The family played at fish fries around the city, licensed by permit, where supper was charged and men treated the women.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, they had a regular family get together, but every year they would all match. They had their own group. They'd get together. And that was string music. Then on Saturday night, it was fish fries. You know, Saturday night fish fries, they would go in them fish fries, and they would entertain in them fish fries. At that time, very few people could play piano, but probably every horn had a piano if they couldn't play a piano, but they had pianos in the horn. But they would perform a guitar. So on the other hand, when they have a fish fry, well, all night we call them fish fries and Saturday night guitars, but they all would meet up in them fish fries. And they would play that, you know?

A lot of times, all over the city they used to have fish fries. And they would have a white eye, a red light. And these guitar players, they'd make all these fish fries. And they would play, and people would be in there. And they would play up music, and they'd sing, and they'd dance by the guitar. And dancing in there too. That's right. That's right.
And that was the people just, what did they, how did they, how did they make that thing pay? I mean, did the people, were they charged so much to go in, or did they just donate for a kitty, or?

Well, it wasn't nothing to go in, but you would have to have a permit. You see, the city would give you a permit for that. And then they would come and pick up the permit. And on the autumn night, then later hours, I mean, after they picked up the permit, well, they all would get together and they would have a nice time with the music. But then if they stayed too late, then it disturbed, well, they would come back. But the idea wasn't to make money then? Well, no, it wasn't make money, but I mean, money was more plentiful. But if a fellow would come in, and they would have people come there, well, they wouldn't treat one, they would treat everybody.
Yeah. Were they charged for the dinner?

But a fellow would come in, the fish fries, there was 10 or 15 women in there. Well, they would treat them all. Yeah. It's like the old time dancing. Whenever you go to dance, well, they'd play something in there, they'd play a march. On the autumn, when they'd play that march, well, everybody would march up and have to buy the ladies something. So that's what they'd do on the fish fries. And the fellow would come in to the fish fries, they'd have people just come there, they'd have a nice coach, and be at the fish fries. Well, when they'd treat, they would treat everybody in there.
